rubric: CDN: static and cacheable pages, TTL/purge, edge
app cache: hot objects, cache-aside, stampede protection

failure modes (stampede, cold cache, stale data)
combined recommendation

prompt: Our SaaS startup has $2.0M ARR growing 8% month over month, an 85% gross margin, a net burn of $300k per month and $3.0M in the bank. Analyze: (1) the runway if burn stays flat and if burn grows 5% per month, (2) ARR after 12 months at the current growth rate and if growth decays to 4% month over month, (3) the main unit-economics risks we should check, and (4) when we should start fundraising. Show the key calculations.

rubric: runway flat burn = 10 months
runway with 5%/month burn growth ~ 8 months (sum 300k*1.05^k reaches 3M after ~8.1 months)
ARR after 12 months at 8% ~ $5.04M
decay scenario computed and lower
unit economics risks: CAC payback, churn/NRR, LTV/CAC, margin
fundraising timing ~ start 6-9 months before cash-out, i.e. now/very soon

prompt: Evaluate the security of a public REST API with these properties: API keys are passed in the URL query string, there is no rate limiting, error responses include stack traces and SQL fragments, CORS allows any origin with credentials, and the /admin endpoints are protected only by an X-Admin: true header. Explain the risk of each issue, how it could be exploited, and give a prioritized remediation plan.

rubric: keys in query strings leak via logs/referrers/history; move to Authorization header + rotation
no rate limiting: brute force / abuse / DoS; add per-key limits
verbose errors leak internals aiding SQLi; generic errors + logging
CORS * with credentials (browsers block wildcard+credentials but reflected origins are dangerous); allowlist
X-Admin header trivially spoofable: critical; real authZ
prioritized plan with admin auth first
